question.leadin: Answer the following about World War I.
question.text: Led by Franz Joseph the First, this dual-monarchy declared war on Serbia in July 1914.
question.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary (accept Austro-Hungarian Empire/Monarchy; do not prompt on partial answer)
question.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

swap.text: What nephew of Franz Josef was killed in that attack?
swap.answerHtml: Archduke Franz Ferdinand [or Francis Ferdinand; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

question.text: A Congress in this Austrian city attempted to create a "balance of power" in Europe after Napoleon's defeat.
question.clue: This city's St. Stephen's Cathedral features a distinctive tiled roof characterized by its colored zigzag pattern and prominent double-headed eagles.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about scandals in the French Third Republic.
swap.text: This Austrian reporter's experiences of anti-Semitism in the Dreyfus affair and elsewhere led him to plan the First Zionist Conference.
swap.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the 1814 and 1815 Congress of Vienna.
question.text: The Congress was chaired by this Austrian who pushed for the Carlsbad Decrees and was forced to resign in 1848.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.leadin: In the 18th century, Austria was not exactly friendly to the idea of a female ruler.
swap.text: Name this Austrian ruler whose father Charles VI attempted to facilitate her ascension to the throne with the passage of the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713.
swap.clue: To govern compulsory peasant labor, this monarch issued the Robot Patent.

question.leadin: Members of this family were elected to the Holy Roman Emperorship continuously from 1493 to 1740.
question.text: Name this dynasty of central and western Europe, which split into Austrian and Spanish branches in 1556.
question.clue: In the 19th century, this family took the title "King of Lombardy-Venetia".

swap.text: This woman took power in 1740 following the 1713 Pragmatic Sanction. Her son Joseph II attempted reforms like abolishing serfdom, but died at the age of 39.
swap.clue: This leader lost control of Silesia when the Pragmatic Sanction, set up by her father, Charles VI, was violated by Prussia.

question.leadin: After World War II, this event led to the formation of the "victim theory."
question.text: Name this event translated as "connection" that Karl Schuschnigg failed to prevent. An original language term is required.
question.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

swap.text: The over-the-top Soviet war memorial in Schwarzenbergplatz in this country's capital city has been targeted by vandals, but it is protected by the 1955 treaty by which Soviet troops ended their occupation of part this country.
swap.clue: This country's far-right Freedom Party was led by Jorg Haider (yerg "HI"-der).

question.leadin: Paul McCartney led a 30-superstar "Rockestra" during relief concerts for Cambodia at this politician's suggestion.
question.text: Name this politician who was the target of an expose written by Alfred Worm for Profil magazine. This leader succeeded U Thant ("ooh tant") as United Nations Secretary General.
question.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

swap.leadin: It began when the arrival of Wehrmacht troops met with ecstatic pro-German crowds in March, 1938, and was followed by Hitler's call for the Sudeten from Czechoslovakia.
swap.text: Name this union between Austria and Germany which was prohibited by the Treaty of Versailles.
swap.clue: This action ended the political career of Wilhelm Miklas, who served as president of the nation in which it occurred.

question.text: Before Balfour, Joseph Chamberlain worked with this man to establish a temporary Jewish homeland in the Uganda Scheme. This founder of Zionism discussed the "Jewish Question" in his 1895 pamphlet Der Judenstaat ("dare YOO-den-shtaht").
question.clue: With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man.

swap.leadin: In a 1783 declaration issued at Czernowitz, this Holy Roman Emperor abolished slavery in the Bukovina.
swap.text: Name this emperor whose Patent of Toleration granted Christians religious freedom, which was extended to Jews in the Edict of Tolerance. This emperor's inebriated soldiers drank schnapps during a disaster at Karansebes ("KAW-rahn-seb-esh").
swap.clue: His first wife Isabella of Parma died of smallpox long before that blunder in the Battle of Karansebes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about assassinations throughout history.
question.text: The 1914 assassination of this Austrian archduke by the Black Hand in Sarajevo served as the impetus for the formation of the Triple Alliance and Triple Entente powers.
question.clue: It's 1914. You are a Bosnian Serb and member of the Black Hand Gavrilo Princip, who will assassinate this Archduke and his wife Sophie, setting off a chain of events that will begin World War I.

swap.text: Empress Elisabeth built the Achilleion ("ah-KILL-ee-on") after this event. This event was named after the hunting lodge where her son Rudolf died, after the Habsburg family learned of his affair with the young Baroness Mary Vetsera.
swap.clue: Ida von Ferenczy was drafted to break the news of this event to Empress Elizabeth.

question.text: This statesman examined the herbalist Magda Logomer, whose 1757 acquittal ended Croatian witch trials. A report by this physician of Maria Theresa led to the prohibition of anti-vampire superstitious practices.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the short-lived Duchy of Warsaw.
swap.text: This 1809 treaty assigned Krakow and Lublin to the Duchy, and compelled Austria to pay a large indemnity to France and break off trade relations with England.

question.text: This man replaced Metternich as Austria's chief minister, orchestrated the abdication of Ferdinand I, and attempted to restore the absolutist rule of the Hapsburgs as advisor to Franz Joseph I.

swap.text: The War of Austrian Succession was fought over the right of this monarch to ascend to the Austrian throne, which went against Salic Law and was supported by the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713.
